project.description: The half of issue 155 that was left out of scope there. That fix taught the reflective walk over the test class to key an unqualified @Inject as @Default, matching what ProcessInjectionPoint reports, but writing @Any out by hand on a test-class field still produced a key of {@Any} against the bean side's {@Default} - two synthetic beans for one type and AmbiguousResolutionException again. @Any never narrows a resolution, because every bean holds it implicitly, so it has no business in the key at all. Normalization now happens inside IpKey rather than at either call site, which is what stops the two paths drifting apart a third time. This scenario pins every spelling of the same request onto one mock, and pins that a real qualifier still separates them.
project.name: jawelte tests/cdi-module scenario 68: @Any never splits an auto-mock
